name: AmphibiNFT App
tagline: A Web3 NFT app for Amphibians that allows users to upload or take photos of amphibians, mint them as NFTs.
description:
AmphibiNFT is an AI-powered NFT dApp that allows users to upload images of amphibians (specifically iguanas and salamanders) and mint them as Flow-based NFTs—but only if they're biologically valid. Leveraging a custom-trained computer vision model, FroggyAI brings together AI automation, real-time image classification, and smart contract-driven minting into a fun, modular application that bridges the physical world and the blockchain.

💡 What It Does:
🖼️ Upload: User selects or drops an image.
🧠 Classify: A backend AI model identifies whether it's an iguana (Class 0) or salamander (Class 1).
✅ Gatekeeping: Only images correctly classified are eligible to mint NFTs.
🪙 Mint: The app mints an NFT on the Flow blockchain, embedding image metadata and species classification.
🖼️ View: Users can retrieve and display their NFT collection via the frontend dashboard.

🛠️ Technologies Used:
Frontend: Next.js (React), Flow Wallet Integration (FCL)
Backend: Custom AI model (Python API), classification logic
Blockchain: Flow blockchain (Cadence smart contracts, Flow JS SDK)
Storage: Currently centralized image URLs; planning to extend with Filecoin/IPFS for decentralized metadata and media storage
Deployment: Vercel

🎯 Alignment with PL_Genesis:
✅ Track: AI & Autonomous Infrastructure
FroggyAI automates classification → validation → NFT minting.
✅ Sponsor Bounty: Flow
Core logic is built on Flow, using custom Cadence contracts with metadata views and admin roles.
✅ Modular Design:
Components (AI model, frontend, NFT logic) are decoupled and composable.
⚠️ Future Integration:
Planning to incorporate Filecoin/IPFS for full decentralization and verifiable on-chain metadata referencing.

📈 Future Enhancements:
🧬 Support more amphibian species
📦 Store all image and metadata on IPFS/Filecoin
🌿 Add rarity traits or breeding mechanics to NFTs
📊 Include audit trail for AI model inference (e.g., IPFS-stamped logs)
